frame.stacking: four 0.14 m corner posts carry the load; flat top at y=1.2 and flat foot at y=0; the outer box is exactly the bounds (iron post bands flush with it, posts 4 mm inside), so bounding-box corner snap points stack one pallet on another; the upper pallet's skids and side sills land on the lower one's top beams. 1.20 high = the low Metal Rack: two pallets stacked are as tall as the tall rack. The contents sit inside the opening of the top frame (inside the posts and beams in plan) and stay below y = 1.17.
frame.heavy: r3: posts 0.14 (r2 0.09), top beams 0.13 deep (r2 0.06), skids 0.16 x 0.10, deck planks 0.05, timber X braces on the back, 0.10 wide iron straps on the sides, riveted brackets and plates

space.unity: prefab space, origin on the floor at the centre of the footprint, +z front, +y up, +x to the furniture's left seen from the front

fill_order: NOT mirrored: units are listed in fill order, the n-th stack goes to unit n. Lowest tier first (units 0-15 tier 0, 16-31 tier 1, 32-47 tier 2, 48-63 tier 3); per tier the back row then the front, each row left to right seen from the front. A tier is full before the next one starts, so nothing floats. Leave mirror off for this store.
position: unit position = bottom centre of its pile, 1 mm over the deck (tier 0) or over the top bar of the tier below. box_size = [x, y, z] Unity, informational.
copy_rule: Each copy = one bar at TRUE SIZE: align (long axis -> +z on tiers 0 and 2, into the depth; -> +x on tiers 1 and 3, across; thin axis -> up), then_rotate (a little yaw, the top bar sometimes turned end for end), fit_longest_m 0.6226 = the vanilla bar's own longest side, so scale 1.000; anchor bottom. Layer j sits at offset.y = j * 0.1249 m. 2 bars per unit, bottom first.

all_bars.note: Copper, Tin, Bronze, Iron, Silver, BlackMetal, Flametal and FlametalNew share one 44-triangle bar mesh

layout.tiers_0_2: 8 across x 2 deep, bars along the depth
layout.tiers_1_3: 4 across x 4 deep, bars along the width
